reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews/Israelites as followers of Yahweh in multiple ways: (1) Moses and Aaron consistently refer to 'Yahweh, God of Israel' and 'the God of the Hebrews' as their deity; (2) The Hebrews repeatedly express their intention to serve and sacrifice to Yahweh: 'we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God' (וְנִזְבְּחָה לַיהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ); (3) The narrative shows Yahweh performing miracles specifically to liberate the Hebrews from Egypt and enable them to worship Him; (4) The Hebrews desire to journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices and serve Yahweh, indicating religious devotion and obedience.
